title: Measurement Units and Conversion
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Measurement Units and Conversion. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Metric units

The metric system scales by powers of ten: (\(1 km=1000 m\)), (\(1 m=100 cm\)), (\(1 kg=1000 g\)), and (\(1 L=1000 mL\)). Multiply when converting to a smaller unit and divide when converting to a larger unit.

Area and volume

Unit factors are squared for area and cubed for volume: (\(1 m^2=10,000 cm^2\)), while (\(1 m^3=1,000,000 cm^3\)). Since (\(1 L=1000 cm^3\)), a volume conversion cannot use the linear factor alone.

Rates and precision

Write units beside quantities in compound measures, such as (\(km/h\)) or (\(kg/m^3\)). Convert before combining different units. Keep unrounded intermediate values when accuracy matters, then round the final measurement to the required precision.

Worked example: Convert (\(2.4 m^2\)) to square centimetres. Since (\(1 m=100 cm\)), square the factor: (\(1 m^2=10,000 cm^2\)); therefore (\(2.4 m^2=24,000 cm^2\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Write the conversion factor as a fraction so unwanted units cancel.
  • For squared or cubed units, square or cube the entire linear conversion factor.
  • Estimate the order of magnitude to catch misplaced decimal points.
  • Convert minutes to hours before using a speed in kilometres per hour.
  • Use a consistent precision and round only at the end.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• (\(1 hour=60 minutes=3600 seconds\)); (\(1 day=24 hours\)).
  • (\(1 hectare=10,000 m^2\)); (\(1 km^2=1,000,000 m^2\)).
  • Temperature: (\(F=(9/5)C+32\)); temperature differences use (\(\Delta F=(9/5)\Delta C\)).
  • Mass and weight are different physical quantities, though everyday contexts may use 'weight' informally.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Convert (\(2.5\text{ km}\)) to metres.

    1. (\(250\text{ m}\))
    2. (\(2,050\text{ m}\))
    3. (\(2,500\text{ m}\))
    4. (\(25,000\text{ m}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(2,500\text{ m}\))

    Multiply by 1,000: (\(2.5\cdot1,000=2,500\text{ m}\)).

  2. Core:

    Convert (\(3.2\text{ kg}\)) to grams.

    1. (\(32\text{ g}\))
    2. (\(320\text{ g}\))
    3. (\(3,200\text{ g}\))
    4. (\(32,000\text{ g}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3,200\text{ g}\))

    Since (\(1\text{ kg}=1,000\text{ g}\)), (\(3.2\text{ kg}=3,200\text{ g}\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Convert (\(3.6 km\)) to metres.

    1. (\(36 m\))
    2. (\(360 m\))
    3. (\(3600 m\))
    4. (\(36,000 m\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(3600 m\))

    Multiply by 1000: (\(3.6 \times 1000=3600 m\)).

  4. Standard:

    Convert (\(0.75 L\)) to millilitres.

    1. (\(75 mL\))
    2. (\(750 mL\))
    3. (\(7500 mL\))
    4. (\(0.075 mL\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(750 mL\))

    Since (\(1 L=1000 mL\)), (\(0.75 L=750 mL\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Convert (\(2.5 m^3\)) to litres.

    1. (\(250 L\))
    2. (\(2500 L\))
    3. (\(25,000 L\))
    4. (\(2,500,000 L\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(2500 L\))

    One cubic metre is 1000 litres. Thus (\(2.5 m^3=2500 L\)).
